# Wave Kit

Wave Kit is Jay Hack's open React design system for jay.ai and personal
projects. It emphasizes simplicity, legibility, classic math and physics
diagrams, and 1960s Japanese poster art, especially Kazumasa Nagai.

## Install the agent skill

npx skills add jayhack/wave-kit --skill build-with-wave-kit -y

Skill source:
https://github.com/jayhack/wave-kit/tree/main/plugin/wave-kit/skills/build-with-wave-kit

Raw skill instructions:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jayhack/wave-kit/main/plugin/wave-kit/skills/build-with-wave-kit/SKILL.md

## Install the React package

npm install @jayhack/wave-kit tailwindcss

To contribute to Wave Kit itself, install from a checkout:

git clone https://github.com/jayhack/wave-kit.git
npm install ./wave-kit/packages/wave-kit tailwindcss

Then import both stylesheets once:

@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@jayhack/wave-kit/styles.css";

## Main exports

WaveField, FluidAnimation, NavigationIndex, BackLink, GitHubButton, TextLink,
Tabs, Divider, ProgressiveImage, ImageCard, Lightbox, CodeBlock, EditableTitle,
EditableText, ExperimentIndex, ExperimentPage, ExperimentHeader,
ExperimentMetrics, ExperimentMeta, and parseExperiments.

## Experiment registry

Register research experiments as a JSON array of ExperimentRecord objects:
slug, title, description, an optional date string, optional metrics
[{ label, value }], optional meta string map, and an optional href. Validate
loaded JSON with parseExperiments. Render the registry with ExperimentIndex —
a compact list of linked rows with the title, a quiet sans-serif date beside
it, a one-line description, and a gray chevron; each row links to
/experiments/<slug> by default, or the record's href. Render each experiment
page with ExperimentPage, which draws the header, metrics table, and metadata
footer from the record while its children remain free-form: figures,
rollouts, or page-specific interactive code. Never add uppercase eyebrow
labels or per-row metrics to the index.

## Design rules

Use a black canvas with signal blue, heat red, energy orange, and light yellow.
Use native system sans for display, heading, body, subtle text, and labels.
Use the platform monospace stack for code and color tokens. Keep controls
rectangular with modest radii. Keep hover changes immediate. Use original
images with progressive loading and the package Lightbox.

ImageCard is the default compact image-led link: edge-to-edge golden-ratio
media, one title line, no more than two detail lines, and equal row heights.

Default to a blog-post reading model with vertical scrolling, semantic
sections, paragraphs, and images or interactive assets interspersed with the
text they support. Avoid decorative eyebrows, sequence numbers, badges, and
labels that merely repeat nearby content. Keep titles proportional and avoid
oversized hero text. Remove anything that adds no meaning, navigation, or
function.

## Code and documentation

The homepage contains working React examples for the global stylesheet, wave
field, navigation index, progressive image lightbox, and named Tailwind colors.

Source repository:
https://github.com/jayhack/wave-kit

Current live documentation:
https://wave-kit.dev

Canonical design reference:
https://jay.ai/design
